name: University of St Andrews

settingEvidence.evidence: The town of St Andrews provides a unique and picturesque location for our very special university.

fees.text: £10,050 a year for students from England (rest-of-UK fee status) on courses starting in September 2027, yet to be confirmed by the UK Government. The fee for 2026-27 is expected to be £9,790. You pay fees every year you attend (four years for most degrees) and fees may increase annually.

source.evidence: England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland, Channel Islands, Isle of Man: £10,050 (yet to be confirmed by the UK Government)

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £5,847 to £12,976 for the year (contracts of 34 to 38 weeks), including utilities and internet. Catered halls include meals (14 or 19 a week); typical self-catered en suite rooms are about £8,001 to £9,652. Prices are the 2026-27 fees on the page.

source.evidence: Studio apartment, shared occupancy £5,847

openDays.text: Next visiting days: 28 October 2026 in person (fully booked) and 4 November 2026 online. In 2027: in person on 14 April; online on 28 April, 19 May and 23 June. In-person Talk and Tour visits run on Mondays and Fridays.

source.evidence: Wednesday 14 April 2027 - in person visiting day - Bookings will open Monday 1 March 2027 at 12.05pm.

contextual.summary: UK applicants with one or more widening-access indicators (such as a low-participation postcode, a school with low progression, a listed access programme, or care experience) are considered against lower 'Minimum' entry grades. It does not guarantee an offer.
contextual.typicalReduction: Each course page publishes lower 'Minimum' grades for widening access students, e.g. Economics A-levels ABB instead of AAA.

criteria.detail: Your home postcode is in the lowest 40% of the Scottish (SIMD) or English, Welsh or Northern Irish (IMD) deprivation indexes. ACORN data is also used.
You attend or most recently attended a school or college with low progression to higher education or low attainment, using school-level data for your nation.

You took part in a widening access programme: Sutton Trust Summer School, LEAPS, Focus West, Lift Off, Aspire North, Reach, Fife First Chances Programme or the Scottish Wider Access Programme (SWAP). The policy also mentions University of St Andrews outreach programmes and government-supported initiatives.
Care experienced or looked after, verified with evidence. Care-experienced applicants are also covered by the University's offer pledge.
Young carer or caring responsibilities, verified with evidence.
Estranged from family, verified with evidence.
Refugee, asylum seeker or displaced person, verified with evidence.
From a group known to be under-represented in higher education or known to have faced disadvantage (for example Gypsy, Traveller, Roma, Showman and Boater communities), subject to verification.

contextual.rulesText: Standard: applications where no contextual indicators have been identified. Minimum: applications where one or more contextual indicators have been identified. Contextual information is collated centrally for applicants with Home or rest-of-UK (RUK) fee status, and the University's online entry indicator shows which category applies. Contextual information alone does not result in an automatic offer. The University pledges an offer to first-degree applicants who declare a looked after or care experienced background (or who live in the most deprived 20% of Scotland and attend a school with lower than average progression), if they show they want to study the subject and meet the entry requirements at the first attempt.

source.evidence: Minimum: applications where one or more contextual indicators have been identified.

programmes.whoCanApply: Students who will be 16 to 18 years old on arrival, applying with an academic transcript showing strong GCSE grades, A grades or a minimum 3.2 GPA (or equivalent), an academic reference and a short personal statement.
